solution.what: Fetched DECODE R473 record page, transcription DOC_R473_D3610 and images 3612-3614 with the project cookie (fetch_img.py).
Read DECODE's transcription: Hungarian clear text with numerical cipher runs, each run under a contemporary interlinear gloss.
Checked images 3612 and 3614: the interlinear decipherment is in a contemporary hand over nearly every group; endorsement '1706 I. 9' and closing 'Kilencedik Januarii' date the letter 9 Jan 1706.
Pencil note 'H.o. R.I. 102 a 1 jegyzet. 494. p.' identified as Raday Pal iratai I (1955) item 102 n. 1 p. 494; Szaktars copy paywalled (403), not checked.
Hard-EM alignment of cipher runs with DECODE's transcription of the glosses (align.py) to rebuild the key: too noisy, 154/373 groups in mismatched runs; key not rebuilt.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked DECODE's transcription with its interlinear-gloss lines; a clean transcription of the gloss is missing

texts.label: R473, 9 Jan 1706
texts.summary: László Vetési Kökényesdi, as 'Cassimirus Miloftzki', to Ferenc Rákóczi II, 9 January 1706, in Hungarian with numerical cipher runs; the interlinear glosses name France, Italy, Spain, Holland and England, November and December, and Ráday in the third person.
texts.note: DECODE's transcription (MA, 2020) holds both the cipher and, in its PLAINTEXT lines, a poor transcription of the contemporary interlinear decipherment. A clean transcription of the gloss is project work; Ráday Pál iratai I (1955) item 102 n. 1 was not checked. Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: the PLAINTEXT lines are garbled Hungarian between cipher numbers ('n a gy i o hglpnd', 'Foad orh. Bn l er g po s ta ad ok ot Nagod'); no sentence can be built from the file.
